text.insert: Workers receive accepted, worker-facing standards as instructions for authored source. Checks then evaluate their output. A standard should identify its lint rules or its review mechanism so a reader can tell which requirements are automatically enforced.

steps.text: Include the worker-facing rules in boot context
Run associated lint checks against the proposed source changes
Review requirements without automated checks explicitly
Preserve findings and gate the handoff on the required checks

text.insert: and fails closed if the scanner cannot run. Worker-side checks and the regression-check gate use that scanner. A declared standard or accepted status alone does not create an automated lint rule.

Librarians see standards for recognition so a mandated code shape is not mistaken for an inferred developer convention. They do not publish or change standards through semantic proposals. A person authors and reviews those changes.

rows: The <decomp_standards> prompt block: accepted, worker-facing standards with their do and do_not signals; condensed to five rules at the compact budget and two at minimal
Enforced, not injected: review_lint findings carry the violated standard_id; the scan fails closed
Recognition only: id, title, summary of accepted standards, so a standard-mandated code shape is not mistaken for a developer convention
GET /api/standards returns records, examples, the effective XML, context, inventory, and warnings; POST applies one validated edit
